title: Key format
description: The format of the text of a key. The protocol defines no format (protocol 3.8), so the tool keycheck reads it as an input. The text is a prefix, a random part and an optional checksum. A schema cannot check the rules between members, for example that the alphabet has each digit of the encoding. The tool keycheck checks them.

prefix.description: The text at the start of each key. It has 1 to 32 printable ASCII characters.

length.description: The number of characters of the whole text, the prefix included.

alphabet.description: The characters that can follow the prefix, the checksum included. A range has the form x-y. A hyphen at the start or at the end is a character. No character occurs two times.

checksum.description: The checksum at the end of the text. A format without this member has no checksum.

algorithm.description: crc32 is the CRC-32 of zlib.

encoding.description: base62 uses the digits 0-9, A-Z and a-z. hex uses the digits 0-9 and a-f. The most significant digit is first.

characters.description: The number of characters of the checksum. The encoder adds the digit zero on the left up to this number.

covers.description: The text that the checksum covers. The default is random.
